title: Why You Should Be Openly Friendly On The First Day Of School https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2018/08/11/be-openly-friendly-on-the-first-day-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin directly refutes the persistent advice to withhold smiling for the first month of school, arguing that students only see a teacher as a pushover when the teacher fails to follow through on stated expectations—not because the teacher was kind. He lists numerous specific benefits of openly friendly behavior on day one, including building instant rapport, modeling positive interaction, signaling safety to nervous students, reducing excitability, making consequences matter more, and triggering the law of reciprocity so students want to return kindness with good behavior. He also notes secondary effects, such as parents becoming allies once their children come home enthusiastic about a new teacher. Ultimately, he states his number-one goal on the first day isn't flawless routines but that students love coming to his classroom, since that single ingredient makes everything else work.
points: Linsin refutes the common advice to withhold smiling for the first weeks of school, arguing pushover status comes from failing to follow through, not from kindness.
A long list of specific benefits of first-day friendliness is offered, including rapport-building, modeling positive interaction, and signaling safety to nervous students.
Friendliness is said to reduce excitability, one of the biggest causes of misbehavior, and to make later consequences matter more to students.
The law of reciprocity is invoked: when students realize they like a teacher, they want to return that kindness through better behavior.
Linsin states his true number-one first-day goal is not flawless routines but that students genuinely love coming to his classroom.
quotes: Surprisingly, it’s still common advice: Never smile the first month or two of the school year.
The truth is, your students will only view you as a pushover if you fail to do what you say you’re going to do.
A warm and welcoming manner draws students to you. It causes them to want to be around you and get to know you better, which in turn builds fast, easy, and natural rapport .
Because it puts students at ease, a calm and friendly nature virtually eliminates excitability , which is one of the biggest causes of misbehavior—especially among your most challenging students.
When students first realize that they like their new teacher, their appreciation creates a strong desire to return your kindness. It makes them want to listen to you, behave for you, and please you.
My number one goal on that first day isn’t that my students can perform every routine perfectly. It’s that they love coming to my classroom.
